traditional_uses: Used in Ayurveda. Small human studies of prepared extracts have studied stress and sleep, but further research is needed.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Reported adverse effects include nausea, headache and agitation.
tulsi.notice: Small studies do not establish treatment efficacy. Leaf identification cannot establish an extract's composition.

traditional_uses: Neem has a history of traditional medicinal use. This does not establish clinical benefit or safe consumption.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Do not ingest neem oil. Serious poisoning has been reported, particularly in children.
Long-term leaf consumption may carry risks; do not self-treat using a photo identification.
neem.notice: Evidence and safety depend on the plant part and preparation. This historical reference is not clinical proof.

traditional_uses: Historically used in several traditional medicine systems, including Ayurveda, for indigestion and other conditions. This is historical use, not a treatment recommendation.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Medicinal evidence usually concerns rhizome or prepared extracts, not a leaf photo.
Some highly bioavailable curcumin products have been linked to liver injury. Turmeric supplements may be unsafe during pregnancy.
turmeric.notice: NCCIH says evidence is not sufficient for definitive conclusions about health benefits. Leaf identification does not establish the composition or safety of a preparation.

traditional_uses: Used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine. Traditional use is not proof of clinical benefit.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Liver injury has been reported with supplements.
May interact with medicines and may be unsuitable with thyroid or autoimmune disorders. Consult a qualified clinician.
ashwagandha.notice: NCCIH reports evidence for some preparations in stress and insomnia, but evidence varies by preparation and does not establish a benefit from an identified leaf.

traditional_uses: Bacopa has a history of use in Ayurveda for memory. Some small studies of standardized extracts have studied cognition.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
The name Brahmi can also refer to Centella asiatica. This prototype targets Bacopa monnieri only.
Consult a clinician before using supplements; a model prediction cannot establish safety.
brahmi.notice: Research on standardized extracts cannot be transferred to an unidentified leaf or home preparation. This is not a treatment claim.

traditional_uses: Bael has traditional medicinal uses described in reviews. Most reported effects concern laboratory, animal or preparation-specific research.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Do not use a leaf prediction to choose a medicinal preparation or dose. Human safety evidence remains limited.

sources.title: Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Disease: Aegle marmelos overview (2014)

bael.notice: Laboratory and animal findings do not establish clinical benefit or safe dosing in humans.

traditional_uses: Mint plants and peppermint oil have a history of use for digestive complaints. Traditional use is not proof that peppermint leaves treat a condition.
constituents: Menthol is present in peppermint oil; composition is not measured by this app.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Evidence on enteric-coated peppermint oil is not evidence for using a raw leaf.
Peppermint oil can cause heartburn, irritation or allergic reactions. Do not apply it to the face of infants or young children.
peppermint.notice: NCCIH reports very little research on peppermint leaf and insufficient evidence to determine its usefulness for any health condition.

traditional_uses: The EMA recognizes traditional use of prepared melissa leaf medicines for mild stress, sleep and mild digestive symptoms.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
The EMA summary concerns specific leaf preparations, not any freshly identified plant.
Discuss supplements with a clinician, especially for children, pregnancy, breastfeeding or when taking medicines.
lemon_balm.notice: EMA conclusions are based on long-standing traditional use, not sufficient clinical-trial evidence. This is educational information, not instructions for use.

traditional_uses: Stevia-derived high-purity steviol glycosides are used as sweeteners. Sweetener use is not evidence of medicinal benefit.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.

The US FDA distinguishes high-purity glycosides from whole leaves and crude extracts, which are not permitted as conventional-food sweeteners in the US. This is a US regulatory distinction, not an Indian approval statement.

sources.title: US FDA: Aspartame and Other Sweeteners in Food

stevia.notice: Purified sweeteners and whole leaves are different products. No diabetes-treatment claim is made.

traditional_uses: Catnip has traditional uses, but human clinical evidence for medicinal use is limited.
safety_notes: Identification aid only. Do not consume or use based on a model prediction.
Avoid medicinal use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Excessive ingestion may cause headache, malaise or vomiting. A model prediction cannot establish safety.
catnip.notice: Limited human data do not establish medicinal benefit or dosing. Insect-repellent research on preparations does not validate consuming leaves.
